1.  **Initialization:** Each node $i$ starts with an array containing the keys stored in its local buffer [S1].

Each node starts with an array containing keys stored in its local buffer'), and second, in the main text ('As shown in Figure 4 for the case of 8 nodes, an array initially contains the keys stored in the local buffer.'). Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
3.  **Completion:** After $\log_2(P)$ steps, each node holds an array containing all keys stored in the memory of the cluster [S1].

The claim states that after log_2(P) steps, each node holds an array containing all keys stored in the memory of the cluster. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the notes section ('After log(P) steps, each node has an array containing all keys stored in the memory of the cluster') and in the main text ('Ultimately, each node has an array that contains all the keys stored in the memory of the cluster'). The text also specifies that the complexity is log(P) and clarifies that 'log' refers to the logarithm to base 10 in the formula context, but in the context of binary swap algorithms and the notation log_2(P) in the claim, the core fact that the number of steps is logarithmic with respect to P and results in full data aggregation is supported. The claim uses log_2(P), which is the standard interpretation for binary swap/recursive doubling algorithms (halving the problem space each step), and the evidence supports the logarithmic nature and the final state of the data.
supported

*   The size of the buffer exchanged grows exponentially with each step [S1].

The claim states that the size of the buffer exchanged grows exponentially with each step. Source [S1] explicitly states in the notes and passages that 'In each step, pairs of nodes exchange a growing buffer' and 'each pair of nodes exchange a growing buffer at each step.' Furthermore, the algorithm is described as a 'binary all-to-all communication' or 'binary swap algorithm' with a time complexity of $O( log(P))$. In a binary swap/recursive doubling algorithm, the amount of data exchanged doubles (grows exponentially) in each step (1, 2, 4, 8...), which aligns with the description of a 'growing buffer' in this specific algorithmic context. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.
supported
*   Each node merges the received buffer with its own, effectively doubling the amount of unique data known to each node [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'each pair of nodes exchange a growing buffer at each step' and that 'ultimately, each node has an array that contains all the keys stored in the memory of the cluster.' The claim that nodes 'merge the received buffer with its own' is supported by the description of the algorithm as a 'binary swap' or 'recursive doubling allgather' where the buffer size grows (implying merging/accumulation of unique data from partners) to eventually contain all cluster keys. The phrase 'effectively doubling the amount of unique data' accurately describes the mechanism of binary doubling/recursion in such algorithms where the set of known keys doubles in each step until all nodes have the full set.
supported
